Change c0192. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. I; 1831 Ch. IX.

Context before (unchanged): It is also a duty owed to yourself; for excessive sorrow prevents improvement or enjoyment, or even the discharge of daily usefulness, without which no man is fit for society."

1818 text: This advice, although good, was totally inapplicable to my case; I should have been the first to hide my grief, and console my friends, if remorse had not mingled its bitterness with my other sensations.

1831 text: This advice, although good, was totally inapplicable to my case; I should have been the first to hide my grief, and console my friends, if remorse had not mingled its bitterness, and terror its alarm with my other sensations.

Diff: This advice, although good, was totally inapplicable to my case; I should have been the first to hide my grief, and console my friends, if remorse had not mingled its bitterness {+, and terror its alarm+} with my other sensations.

Context after (unchanged): Now I could only answer my father with a look of despair, and endeavour to hide myself from his view.

result.rationale: Added clause "and terror its alarm" adds a second emotion beside remorse, intensifying Victor's guilt-fear and his inner state. It elaborates feeling without changing events, so expansion fits best, with some characterization of Victor's mental state.
